name: Rani ki Vav
description: Seven-level stepwell built in memory of King Bhima I of the Chaulukya dynasty; over 500 principal sculptures. UNESCO World Heritage Site (2014).

name: Hemchandracharya Jain Gyan Mandir
description: Jain manuscript library in Patan named after the 12th-century polymath Hemacandra, holding thousands of palm-leaf and paper manuscripts.

name: Sun Temple, Modhera
description: Chaulukya-era temple to Surya with a stepped tank (Surya Kund) and richly carved dance hall.

name: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park
description: Pre-Mughal Islamic city, Hindu and Jain temples and fortifications at the foot of Pavagadh hill. UNESCO World Heritage Site (2004).

name: Dholavira: a Harappan City
description: Harappan city on Khadir island with water reservoirs and the famous ten-sign Indus inscription. UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021).

name: Historic City of Ahmedabad
description: Walled city founded by Sultan Ahmad Shah, with pols, gates and Sultanate monuments. India's first World Heritage City (2017).

name: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque
description: Known for its carved stone lattice windows (jali), including the intertwined 'tree of life'.

name: Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad
description: Sultanate-era congregational mosque with 260 pillars blending Hindu, Jain and Islamic styles.

name: Hutheesing Jain Temple
description: Marble temple dedicated to Dharmanatha with a 'Manastambha' and 52 shrines.

name: Dada Harir Stepwell
description: Five-storey stepwell built under the Gujarat Sultanate, with Sanskrit and Arabic inscriptions.

name: Adalaj Stepwell
description: Five-storey octagonal stepwell begun by Rana Veer Singh and completed by Sultan Mahmud Begada.

name: Sabarmati Ashram
description: Mahatma Gandhi's residence during the freedom movement; starting point of the 1930 Dandi March. Holds Gandhi's letters and papers.

name: L. D. Institute of Indology
description: Research institute with one of India's major collections of Jain manuscripts, including the collection of Muni Punyavijayji; museum next door.

name: Akshardham, Gandhinagar
description: Pink sandstone temple complex with exhibitions on Indian culture.

name: Lothal
description: Harappan port town with one of the world's earliest known dockyards; site museum.

name: Somnath Temple
description: First of the twelve Jyotirlingas, on the Arabian Sea coast.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple
description: Five-storey temple to Krishna at the mouth of the Gomti river.

name: Shatrunjaya Hill Temples, Palitana
description: More than 800 Jain temples crowning Shatrunjaya hill, reached by about 3,500 steps.

name: Uparkot Fort, Junagadh
description: Ancient fort with Buddhist caves, the Adi Kadi Vav and Navghan Kuvo stepwells.

name: Ashokan Rock Edicts, Junagadh
description: Granite boulder inscribed with fourteen edicts of Ashoka in Brahmi script, plus later inscriptions of Rudradaman and Skandagupta.

name: Laxmi Vilas Palace
description: Indo-Saracenic residence of the Gaekwads of Baroda.

name: Oriental Institute, M. S. University of Baroda
description: Manuscript library and research institute; publishes the Gaekwad's Oriental Series and holds a large collection of Sanskrit manuscripts.

name: Kirti Mandir, Porbandar
description: Memorial at Mahatma Gandhi's birthplace.

name: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute
description: Home of the critical edition of the Mahabharata and a large collection of Sanskrit and Prakrit manuscripts.

name: Raghunath Temple, Jammu
description: Temple complex whose archives hold Sanskrit manuscripts, including Vedic folios.

name: Saraswathi Mahal Library
description: One of Asia's oldest libraries, with palm-leaf and paper manuscripts in Sanskrit, Tamil, Marathi and Telugu.

name: Asiatic Society of Mumbai
description: Library in Mumbai's Town Hall with rare books, coins and manuscripts.

name: Schoenberg Institute, Penn Libraries
description: Holds Indic manuscripts digitised and openly published, including Vedic Brahmana texts.

name: Royal Danish Library
description: National library of Denmark; its oriental collections include Sanskrit manuscripts in Devanagari.
